question.problem:
The Cartesian equation of the ellipse defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=5\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\sqrt{7}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta <2\pi .
$$

is given by

{{field-1}}
$=1.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the ellipse, we need to eliminate the parameter $\theta .$ We can do this using the Pythagorean theorem.

By isolating the $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{x}{5\sqrt{2}} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{(5\sqrt{2})^{2}} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{50} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

By isolating the $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3\sqrt{7}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{y}{3\sqrt{7}} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{(3\sqrt{7})^{2}} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{63} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations and using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ we get

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{50}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{63}={cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

So, the Cartesian equation of the ellipse is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{50}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{63}=1.
$$
